title: Kirby Problem 4.57
exact_target: Can any two closed oriented smooth four-manifolds with equal Euler characteristic and signature be related by simultaneous surgery on a torus link in the first?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
For a closed oriented smooth $4$-manifold $X$, write
$\chi(X)=\sum_i(-1)^i\dim H_i(X;\mathbb Q)$ for its Euler
characteristic and $\sigma(X)$ for the signature of its intersection
form on $H_2(X;\mathbb R)$. Let $X,Y$ have equal Euler
characteristics and equal signatures.

A torus link in $X$ is a finite disjoint union of smoothly embedded
copies $T_i$ of $T^2=S^1\times S^1$. Require every component to
have trivial normal bundle, and choose disjoint tubular neighborhoods
$\nu T_i\cong T^2\times D^2$. Simultaneous torus surgery removes
their interiors and glues back copies of $T^2\times D^2$ using
chosen boundary diffeomorphisms of $T^3$, with the orientation
convention giving an oriented result.

Is there always such a torus link in $X$ and a choice of gluings
whose result is diffeomorphic to $Y$? If this smooth conclusion is
too strong, does the same assertion hold with ``homeomorphic to $Y$''
in its place?

All surgery tori must already be disjoint in the original $X$.
A sequence in which later tori occur only in a previously altered
manifold would not automatically give the simultaneous surgery asked
for. The number of components and all surgery slopes may depend on
the pair. No simple-connectivity, symplecticity, or prescribed homology
class for the tori is assumed. The numerical equalities are the
hypotheses, not a claimed complete diffeomorphism classification.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Can any two closed oriented smooth four-manifolds with equal Euler characteristic and signature be related by simultaneous surgery on a torus link in the first?
